paper_title: Adapting General-Purpose Embedding Models to Private Datasets Using   Keyword-based Retrieval
caption: Retrieval performance of MAP@10 for different m and sampling strategies.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the retrieval performance, measured as MAP@10, for two distinct sampling strategies — “Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy” (represented by purple bars) and “Uniform Sampling Strategy” (represented by yellow bars) — across five discrete values of the parameter m, ranging from 6 to 10. The horizontal axis (labeled “m”) displays these integer values in ascending order, while the vertical axis (labeled “MAP@10”) spans from 23.0 to 27.0, with major gridlines at intervals of 0.5. For each value of m, two adjacent bars are plotted, allowing direct visual comparison between the two strategies. The Fine-to-Coarse strategy consistently yields higher MAP@10 scores than the Uniform strategy across all m values; for instance, at m=7, the Fine-to-Coarse bar reaches approximately 26.8, while the Uniform bar is around 24.8. The Fine-to-Coarse bars exhibit relatively high and stable performance, peaking at m=7 and slightly declining toward m=10, whereas the Uniform bars show a more variable pattern, with a peak at m=8 (approximately 25.6) and lower values at m=6 and m=10 (both around 24.4). The legend in the upper right corner clearly distinguishes the two strategies by color and label.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the retrieval performance, measured as MAP@10, for two sampling strategies — “Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy” (purple bars) and “Uniform Sampling Strategy” (yellow bars) — across five values of the parameter m (6, 7, 8, 9, and 10). The vertical axis represents MAP@10, ranging from 23.0 to 27.0 with tick marks at 0.5 intervals, while the horizontal axis shows the discrete values of m. For each m, two adjacent bars represent the respective sampling strategies. The Fine-to-Coarse strategy consistently achieves higher MAP@10 scores, ranging from approximately 25.95 (at m=6) to 26.8 (at m=7), peaking at m=7 and showing a slight decline afterward. In contrast, the Uniform strategy scores lower, ranging from about 24.4 (at m=6) to 25.6 (at m=8), with its highest performance also at m=8. The chart includes a legend in the upper right corner identifying the color coding for each strategy, and the bars are grouped by m value with no overlap, allowing for direct visual comparison. The background features light gray gridlines to aid in reading the values. Overall, the Fine-to-Coarse strategy outperforms the Uniform strategy across all tested values of m.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm vergleicht die Retrieval-Leistung, gemessen an MAP@10, für zwei unterschiedliche Sampling-Strategien — „Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy“ (dargestellt durch lila Balken) und „Uniform Sampling Strategy“ (dargestellt durch gelbe Balken) — über fünf diskrete Werte des Parameters m (6, 7, 8, 9, 10), die auf der horizontalen Achse angeordnet sind. Die vertikale Achse zeigt den MAP@10-Wert in einem linearen Skalenbereich von 23.0 bis 27.0, mit Tick-Markierungen in 0.5-Einheiten. Für jede m-Kategorie sind zwei nebeneinander angeordnete Balken zu sehen, wobei der linke Balken die Fine-to-Coarse-Strategie und der rechte Balken die Uniform-Strategie repräsentiert. Die Fine-to-Coarse-Strategie erzielt bei allen m-Werten höhere MAP@10-Werte, die zwischen etwa 25.95 (für m=6) und 26.8 (für m=7) liegen, während die Uniform-Strategie Werte zwischen etwa 24.4 (für m=6) und 25.6 (für m=8) aufweist. Die Balken sind nicht sortiert, sondern nach steigendem m-Wert angeordnet, und es gibt keine visuellen Hervorhebungen wie Schattierungen oder Umrandungen; die Unterschiede zwischen den Strategien sind ausschließlich durch Farbe und Höhe der Balken dargestellt.
